Create a PDF device with embedded fonts

Source: R/portable_pdf.R
portable_pdf.Rd

portable_pdf() opens a PDF graphics device that uses systemfonts and textshaping for font lookup and text layout (the same font stack as the ragg devices) and embeds all used fonts so the document renders the same on any machine.

portable_pdf(
  file = "portable.pdf",
  width = 7,
  height = 7,
  scaling = 1,
  pointsize = 12,
  family = "sans",
  bg = "white",
  metadata = pdf_metadata(),
  colormodel = c("rgb", "gray", "cmyk"),
  compress = TRUE
)

Arguments

file

Path of the file to write to. As with the ragg and svglite devices, the path may contain a sprintf()-style integer format such as "%03d": when it does, each page is written to its own file with the pattern expanded to the page number (starting at 1). Without a format, all pages are written to the single named file. Use "%%" for a literal % when using a format.

width, height

Size of the device in inches.

scaling

A scaling factor applied to the device resolution, in the same way as the scaling argument in ragg and the scale argument in svglite. Values above 1 increase the size of text and other elements relative to the physical page size.

pointsize

Default point size of text.

family

Default font family to use for text.

bg

Background colour of the device. Use "transparent" for no fill.

metadata

Document metadata, created with pdf_metadata().

colormodel

Colour model for output: "rgb" (the default), "gray", or "cmyk". Applies to vector graphics and embedded raster images alike.

compress

Whether to compress the PDF content streams. Set to FALSE to get human-readable content streams, e.g. for debugging the output. Embedded font and image data is always compressed.

Value

Invisibly, the path to the created file.

Examples

portable_pdf(tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"))
plot(sin, -pi, 2 * pi)
dev.off()
